segments.text: The morning after a hard workout, your whole body aches.
You'd think it's lactic acid, but that clears out fast.
But the soreness doesn't start until a day or two later.
Move muscles in an unfamiliar way, and the fibers get tiny tears.
The body triggers inflammation to repair them.
That inflammation irritates the pain nerves, making them extra sensitive.
This repair process takes a day or two.
That's why it hurts more the next day, not right away.
It's the inflammation from repairing the damage that makes you sore for days.
